card.band: 20h tier. Numerically robust simplex plus branching is a large surface. A frontier agent solves the LP and small MIP buckets in some trials, but rarely the harder families. A weaker model stops at the MPS parser and a dense tableau.
card.cheat: There is no HiGHS or scipy in the image and no network. The solution checker is independent. Instances are generated at grading time and the family list is hidden.
card.grading: Hidden set of ~500 generated MIPs (knapsack, set cover, facility location, lot sizing, assignment, infeasible and unbounded cases). Each is checked for status, optimal objective at 1e-6 relative tolerance against HiGHS, and feasibility of the returned solution with an independent checker. Reward is the fraction solved within the limit, and the time limit gives graded credit.
card.reference: A reference solver we write, validated against HiGHS (MIT) offline. Expected size is ~4k lines. Its solve rate on the hidden set is the ceiling.
card.source: MPS format and MIPLIB 2017 (https://miplib.zib.de/, licence not stated, so no MIPLIB files are shipped) ; HiGHS (MIT) as the oracle, version not found
card.task: /app ships the CLI spec and a few small sample MPS/LP models. The agent builds an LP/MIP solver in C++ or Rust: MPS reader (free and fixed format, RANGES and BOUNDS), presolve, dual simplex, branch-and-bound with cuts and heuristics. The CLI prints status and objective plus a solution file under a time limit.

facts.claim: HiGHS core is MIT-licensed; HiPO-enabled binaries and highspy-extras are Apache-2.0
HiGHS latest release is v1.14.0 (April 2026); v1.15 planned for June 2026, not verified as shipped
MIPLIB 2017 benchmark set has 240 instances that are solvable by the union of today's codes
MIPLIB site states no licence or redistribution terms; only a copyright footer (ZIB) and a citation request
MPS format sections (NAME, ROWS, COLUMNS, RHS, RANGES, BOUNDS, ENDATA) and bound types (UP, LO, FX, FR, MI, PL, BV) are documented by solver manuals; free and fixed MPS variants exist
IBM documentation of the MPS format sections and bound types
SCIP is released under Apache-2.0 (a complete permissive MIP solver exists publicly)
CBC is a C++ MIP solver under EPL-2.0 (a complete public MIP solver exists)

No public paper found in which an LLM agent writes a complete MIP solver from scratch with benchmark results; closest work (arXiv 2605.09186, May 2026) extends SCIP plugins and solves five extra MIPLIB instances
Hidden set of ~500 generated MIPs across seven families, checked against HiGHS and an independent checker
Reference solver of ~4k lines exists and is validated against HiGHS

full_card.band: 20h tier. Frontier: some trials pass LP and small MIP families, harder families (lot sizing, big-M facility location, numerics) rarely. Weaker model stops at the MPS parser/dense tableau. Band claim unverified (E0).

full_card.deliverable: C++ or Rust LP/MIP solver: MPS reader (free/fixed, RANGES, BOUNDS), presolve, dual simplex, branch-and-bound with cuts/heuristics, CLI with status, objective, solution file under a time limit.

spike_plan.kill_if: Oracle non-deterministic, or two public solvers disagree beyond 1e-6 on more than about 10% of instances (K4), or every family is either trivial or unsolvable within the limit (K8/K9).
spike_plan.pass_if: Oracle is deterministic, second solver agrees with HiGHS within 1e-6 on at least 95% of instances, and families spread across easy and hard solve times.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, pip install a pinned HiGHS (highspy) and record the exact version; pin the oracle version in the card.
Write a small generator for each of the seven families (knapsack, set cover, facility location, lot sizing, assignment, infeasible, unbounded), 20 seeds each, and write MPS files.
Solve each instance with HiGHS twice with a fixed time limit and thread count; confirm identical status and objective within 1e-9 relative (determinism).
Solve the same instances with a second public solver (SCIP via pyscipopt or CBC via a binary) and count disagreements beyond 1e-6 relative; a high disagreement rate kills the 1e-6 gate (K4).
Record per-family solve times and rates under 10 s and 60 s to set the partial-credit buckets and check that the harder families are not trivially easy or unsolvable for a dense baseline.
Confirm the spec's status convention for MIP unbounded vs infeasible by checking HiGHS' reported status on the unbounded family.

v1.summary: The MIP solver idea passes the gates on paper: MPS and HiGHS (MIT) are real, the generated grading surface is large, and no gate is failed outright, with lookup partial because public solvers exist but cannot be installed offline. The main risks are unverified difficulty bands (no dated evidence), the 1e-6 objective tolerance against HiGHS, and the reference not yet written, so the spike must check oracle determinism and solver agreement before building.

v2.note: Has a real paper trail: the MPS format is documented in solver manuals, and HiGHS (MIT) can serve as a differential oracle. Instances come from a generator, so the grading surface is unlimited, and no MIPLIB files are shipped. The reference solver (~4k lines) has not been written yet, so the 2-4 day estimate is optimistic and Ref and Build are scored low. Nothing dated backs the band claim, so Band stays at 3 with some K9 risk on the lot-sizing and big-M families. Five review fixes: (1) Fix the HiGHS gap settings: mip_rel_gap=0 or an absolute gap, because the default 1e-4 gap conflicts with the 1e-6 objective check. (2) Spell out the infeasible vs unbounded status convention. (3) Judge alternative optima on objective plus feasibility only, so any valid solution passes. (4) Make the time limits generous, because gVisor wall-clock jitter would otherwise cause infrastructure failures. (5) The spike must check that our reference is not slower than the frontier, since its solve rate sets the ceiling.
